question_text: What is the SI unit of gravitational constant G?
hint: Remember the SI unit of G.
easy_answer: G has SI unit N m²/kg².

question_text: State Newton’s universal law of gravitation.
Write the formula for gravitational force between two masses.
What is acceleration due to gravity near Earth’s surface?
Does the value of g change with height above Earth?
hint: Greater distance from Earth’s centre means weaker gravity.

question_text: Define free fall.
easy_answer: Free fall is motion under gravity alone.

question_text: What is weight of an object?
Why is mass constant while weight can change?
easy_answer: Weight changes with g, mass does not.

question_text: What is escape velocity?
easy_answer: It is the minimum speed needed to escape gravity.

question_text: What happens to weight of an object on the Moon compared with Earth?
hint: Moon’s g is about 1/6 of Earth’s.
easy_answer: Moon weight ≈ one-sixth of Earth weight.

question_text: Why do astronauts appear weightless in an orbiting spacecraft?
easy_answer: They are in free fall together.

question_text: State the relation between g and G for a spherical Earth.
hint: M is Earth’s mass and R its radius.

question_text: If distance between two masses is doubled, what happens to gravitational force?
If one mass is doubled while distance remains same, what happens to force?
hint: Force is directly proportional to each mass.

question_text: What is thrust?
easy_answer: Thrust is force acting perpendicular to a surface.

question_text: Define pressure.
What is the SI unit of pressure?
hint: One pascal is one newton per square metre.

question_text: Why does a sharp nail enter wood easily?
State Archimedes’ principle.
easy_answer: Upthrust equals weight of displaced fluid.

question_text: Why does an iron ship float?
hint: Floating depends on average density and buoyancy.
easy_answer: The ship floats when buoyant force balances its weight.
